persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Grace, 66, a retired teacher and volunteer trustee at Hope Community Church, a small church in Texas. A trustee looks after the church building and its money. Last year the church paid a fine because nobody remembered the fire extinguisher check, and today the pastor has asked you to put every important date in one place.

challenge.intro: Now you are Grace, the trustee. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press — use what you learned. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Ahead of It · Church with the normal link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If it does not show, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. The page reloads. If a dark screen says 'Everyone has a list of things…', tap 'I'll explore on my own' at the bottom. You now see an empty list ('empty' at the top). If a small 'Got it ✓' box appears when you open a tab, just tap it.

tasks.text: Put the fire extinguisher service on your list. This year the company is coming on 20 November 2026 — make that its date.

tasks.hint: It is in the Library under Safety & inspections. After adding it, open it on the Next page and change 'Next due', then Save.

tasks.text: Put the church van registration on your list, and make sure the Treasurer (the person who keeps the church money) is told about it.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('steward_v1')||'null');if(!d||!d.items)return false;var f=function(s){return d.items.filter(function(i){return String(i.id).indexOf('djex')!==0&&String(i.n||'').toLowerCase().indexOf(s)>=0})[0]};var i=f('van registration');return !!i&&String(i.who||'').toLowerCase().indexOf('treasurer')>=0;}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Add it from the Library (Vehicles). Open it and look for the box 'Who else needs to know'.

tasks.text: The church generator is not in the library. Add it yourself: 'Generator service', due 15 January 2027. If it is missed, it costs real money.
tasks.hint: Use the round orange ＋ button. Fill in the name and date, and choose how bad it is to miss.

tasks.text: The boiler inspection was finished today. Put it on your list and tell the app the whole job is done, so it moves to next time.
tasks.hint: Add it from the Library, then find it on the Next page. Saving it is not enough — one of its buttons says the job is finished.

tasks.text: If you are ever away, another person will use this list. Write on it that it belongs to Hope Community Church.
tasks.hint: Look in the Hand-off tab, in the box 'Whose list is this?'. Tap outside the box after typing.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: keeps all the important dates of a church building in one place
reminds you before something is due, so you do not pay a fine or lose insurance
another person can take over using the hand-off list

lines: This is Ahead of It, church edition. In the next few minutes you will see what it is for, who it is for, and how to use it.
Here is the everyday problem. A church building runs on dates. The fire extinguishers need their yearly service. The van needs its registration. The insurance renews once a year.
Usually one volunteer keeps all of that in their head, often a trustee. When that person is busy, sick, or steps down, the dates quietly slip by.
And a missed date costs real money: a fine, a lapsed policy, or a ministry closed until the inspection is done.
Ahead of It is for whoever looks after the building: a trustee, a facilities volunteer, a church administrator, or the pastor of a small church.
The big idea is simple. Every date lives on one calm page, and each item comes with its own reminder steps, starting thirty days before it is due.
At the bottom are four tabs: Next, Year, Library, and Hand-off. The round orange plus button adds something of your own.
Start with Library. It holds twenty-four things churches most often forget, in groups like Safety and inspections, Building, Vehicles, Insurance and legal, and Money and filings.
Each one shows how often it comes around and how costly a miss would be. Tap one your building has, and it goes on your list.
Or tap the gold Quick setup button. It shows the whole library on one screen, with a tick box and a date beside each item.
Tick what is yours, fix any date you know, and tap Save my list. Two or three items is a fine start.
Now the Next tab. This is your main page. It sorts everything by what needs you first.
Overdue is at the top, then Do something now, then Next ninety days, then Later this year. When nothing is overdue, it simply says so.
Each item shows how many days until it is due, and the one step to take right now, like Gather what you need.
When you finish a step, tap step tick. When the whole job is done, tap done tick, and the app moves the date forward to next time, so it repeats by itself.
Something not in the library? Tap the round plus button.
Give it a name and a next due date, choose how often it repeats, and pick how bad a miss would be: No big deal, A hassle, or Costs real money.
You can also note what happens if you miss it, who else needs to know, and where the papers are kept. Then tap Save.
The Year tab shows the next twelve months on one page. Red costs real money, amber is a hassle, and green is no big deal. Print it, or add every date to your calendar.
The Hand-off tab is for the day someone else takes over. It copies or prints one page: what is due, who to tell, and where things are.
It also has Save backup file, because everything lives on this one device. And here you write whose list this is.
Your first two minutes: open Library or Quick setup, tick two or three things your building really has, and put in their real dates.
Then glance at the Next tab once a week. If it says Nothing overdue, you are ahead of it.
Your list stays on this device. There is no account, no cloud, and nothing is sent to anyone.
Ahead of It, church edition costs twenty-nine dollars, once. No subscription.
And the round question mark button has the tour and help, any time. Profits help students in Kenya stay in school.
